bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷七十三 四夷附錄第二: 契丹
title.en: Volume 73: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 2 - Khitan 2
title.raw: 卷七十三 四夷附錄第二: 契丹 Volume 73: Appendix on the Four Barbarians 2 - Khitan 2

sentences.zh: 兀欲，東丹王突欲子也。

translations.literal: Wuyu was the son of the Dongdan King Tuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu was a son of Tuyu, the Dongdan King.

sentences.zh: 突欲奔于唐，兀欲留不從，號永康王。

translations.literal: Tuyu fled to Tang, but Wuyu stayed behind and would not follow; he was styled Prince of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyu defected to Tang, Wuyu remained in Khitan territory and refused to go with him, taking the title Prince of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 契丹好飲人血，突欲左右姬妾，多刺其臂吮之，其小過輒挑目、刲灼，不勝其毒。

translations.literal: The Khitan were fond of drinking human blood; Tuyu's concubines and attendants often pricked their arms for him to suck, and for minor faults he would gouge out eyes or brand and burn them, and they could not endure the cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan custom favored drinking human blood; Tuyu's women and attendants often let him prick their arms and suck the blood, while petty offenses brought gouged eyes, branding, and cautery until they could bear no more.

sentences.zh: 然喜賔客，好飲酒，工畫，頗知書。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in entertaining guests, loved wine, was skilled at painting, and was quite learned in books.
translations.idiomatic: Even so he welcomed guests, loved wine, painted well, and was fairly literate.

sentences.zh: 其自契丹歸中國，載書數千卷，樞密使趙延壽每假其異書、醫經，皆中國所無者。

translations.literal: When he came from the Khitan to China, he brought several thousand volumes of books; Privy Council Commissioner Zhao Yanshou often borrowed his rare books and medical classics, works China did not possess.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Khitan lands to China he carried thousands of books; Zhao Yanshou, the Privy Council commissioner, often borrowed his exotic texts and medical treatises—works none in China had.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，自滑州朝京師，遙領武信軍節度使，食其俸，賜甲第一區，宮女數人。

translations.literal: In the Mingzong era he came from Hua Prefecture to court at the capital, held the post of Military Commissioner of Wuxin in absentia, drew its salary, and was granted a first-rank residence and several palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong he traveled from Hua Prefecture to the capital, held the Wuxin circuit commission in absentia with its stipend, and received a top-grade mansion and several palace women.

sentences.zh: 契丹兵助晉于太原，唐廢帝遣宦者秦繼旻、皇城使李彥紳殺突欲于其第。

translations.literal: When Khitan troops aided Jin at Taiyuan, the deposed Tang emperor sent the eunuch Qin Jimin and Imperial City Commissioner Li Yanshen to kill Tuyu in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: While Khitan forces were aiding Jin at Taiyuan, the deposed Tang emperor sent the eunuch Qin Jimin and Imperial City commissioner Li Yanshen to kill Tuyu in his mansion.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖追封突欲為燕王。

translations.literal: Jin Gaozu posthumously enfeoffed Tuyu as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Jin posthumously enfeoffed Tuyu as Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 德光滅晉，兀欲從至京師。

translations.literal: When Deguang destroyed Jin, Wuyu followed him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Deguang overthrew Jin, Wuyu accompanied him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德光殺繼旻、彥紳，籍其家貲，悉以賜兀欲。

translations.literal: Deguang executed Jimin and Yanshen, registered their household goods, and gave the whole to Wuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang put Jimin and Yanshen to death, inventoried their estates, and bestowed everything on Wuyu.

sentences.zh: 德光死欒城，兀欲與趙延壽及諸大將等俱入鎮州。

translations.literal: Deguang died at Luancheng; Wuyu entered Zhen Prefecture together with Zhao Yanshou and the other great generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang died at Luancheng, Wuyu entered Zhen Prefecture with Zhao Yanshou and the other senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 延壽自稱權知軍國事，遣人求鎮州管鑰于兀欲，兀欲不與。

translations.literal: Yanshou styled himself provisional overseer of military and state affairs and sent men to ask Wuyu for the keys to Zhen Prefecture; Wuyu would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou proclaimed himself provisional overseer of military and state affairs and sent men to demand the keys to Zhen Prefecture from Wuyu, but Wuyu refused.

sentences.zh: 延壽左右曰：「契丹大人聚而謀者詾詾，必有變，宜備之。

translations.literal: Yanshou's attendants said, "The Khitan elders are gathering in council with much clamor—there must be a change; you should prepare for it.
translations.idiomatic: His advisers said, "The Khitan chiefs are meeting in a noisy council—something is surely afoot; you must guard against it.

sentences.zh: 今中國之兵，猶有萬人，可以擊虜；

translations.literal: The Chinese troops here still number ten thousand and can strike the barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Our Chinese forces still number ten thousand and can strike the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 不然，事必不成。

translations.literal: otherwise the affair will certainly fail."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise your plan will never succeed."

sentences.zh: 」延壽猶豫不決。

translations.literal: " Yanshou hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanshou wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 兀欲妻，延壽以為妹，五月朔旦，兀欲召延壽及張礪、李崧、馮道等置酒，酒數行，兀欲謂延壽曰：「妹自上國來，當一見之。

translations.literal: Wuyu's wife—whom Yanshou regarded as his younger sister—on the first day of the fifth month Wuyu summoned Yanshou together with Zhang Li, Li Song, Feng Dao, and others to a banquet; after several rounds of wine Wuyu said to Yanshou, "My wife has come from the Upper State and ought to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month Wuyu invited Yanshou, Zhang Li, Li Song, Feng Dao, and others to drink; after several rounds he said, "My wife has just arrived from the north—she is your sister by marriage and you should meet her.

sentences.zh: 」延壽欣然與兀欲俱入。

translations.literal: " Yanshou gladly entered together with Wuyu.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanshou went in with Wuyu in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 食頃，兀欲出坐，笑謂礪等曰：「燕王謀反，鎖之矣。

translations.literal: After the space of a meal Wuyu came out and sat down, smiling as he said to Li and the others, "The Prince of Yan is plotting rebellion—I have locked him up.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wuyu reappeared and told Li and the rest with a smile, "The Prince of Yan was plotting rebellion; I have put him in chains.

sentences.zh: 諸君可無慮也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen need have no concern.
translations.idiomatic: You need not worry.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「先帝在汴州與我算子一莖，許我知南朝軍國事，昨聞寢疾，無遺命，燕王安得自擅邪？

translations.literal: " He added, "The late emperor at Bianzhou gave me one counting rod and promised I should oversee the Southern Court's military and state affairs; yesterday I heard he was gravely ill and left no testament—how could the Prince of Yan act on his own?"
translations.idiomatic: " He went on, "At Bianzhou the late emperor gave me a single counting rod and promised I would govern the Southern Court's armies and state; when he fell ill without a final order, how could the Prince of Yan seize power on his own?"

sentences.zh: 」礪等罷去。

translations.literal: " Li and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Li and the others took their leave.

sentences.zh: 兀欲召延壽廷立而詰之，延壽不能對。

translations.literal: Wuyu summoned Yanshou to stand in the hall and questioned him; Yanshou could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu had Yanshou brought before him in the hall and interrogated him; Yanshou had no reply.

sentences.zh: 乃遣人監之，而籍其家貲。

translations.literal: He then sent men to guard him and registered his household goods.
translations.idiomatic: He placed guards over him and inventoried his property.

sentences.zh: 兀欲宣德光遺制曰：「永康王，大聖皇帝之嫡孫，人皇王之長子，可於中京即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Wuyu proclaimed Deguang's testament, saying, "The Prince of Yongkang, the Great Sage Emperor's legitimate grandson and the Human Emperor's eldest son, may take the throne at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu announced Deguang's testament: "Prince of Yongkang, legitimate grandson of the Great Sage Emperor and eldest son of the Human Emperor, shall ascend the throne at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 」中京，契丹謂鎮州也。

translations.literal: " The Central Capital is what the Khitan call Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " The Central Capital is what the Khitan call Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣使者告哀於諸鎮。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to announce the mourning to the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to announce the mourning to the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蕭翰聞德光死，棄汴州而北，至鎮州，兀欲已去。

translations.literal: When Xiao Han heard that Deguang was dead, he abandoned Bian Prefecture and went north; reaching Zhen Prefecture, Wuyu had already left.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han, hearing of Deguang's death, abandoned Bian Prefecture and marched north; when he reached Zhen Prefecture, Wuyu was already gone.

sentences.zh: 翰以騎圍張礪宅，執礪而責曰：「汝教先帝勿用胡人為節度使，何也？

translations.literal: Han surrounded Zhang Li's residence with horsemen, seized Li, and rebuked him, saying, "You advised the late emperor not to appoint non-Chinese as military commissioners—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Han ringed Zhang Li's house with cavalry, seized him, and demanded, "Why did you tell the late emperor not to appoint non-Chinese as military commissioners?"

sentences.zh: 」礪對不屈，翰鎖之。

translations.literal: " Li answered without yielding; Han locked him up.
translations.idiomatic: " Li answered without yielding; Han put him in chains.

sentences.zh: 是夕，礪卒。

translations.literal: That evening Li died.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Li died.

sentences.zh: 兀欲為人俊偉，亦工畫，能飲酒，好禮士，德光甞賜以絹數千匹，兀欲散之，一日而盡。

translations.literal: Wuyu was handsome and imposing, also skilled at painting, able to drink heavily, fond of honoring scholars; Deguang had once given him several thousand bolts of silk, which Wuyu distributed until they were gone in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu was tall and striking, painted well, drank heavily, and honored men of letters; Deguang had once given him thousands of bolts of silk, which he gave away until none remained within a day.

sentences.zh: 兀欲已立，先遣人報其祖母述律。

translations.literal: After Wuyu had taken the throne, he first sent word to his grandmother Shulü.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Wuyu first reported to his grandmother Shulü.

sentences.zh: 述律怒曰：「我兒平晉取天下，有大功業，其子在我側者當立，而人皇王背我歸中國，其子豈得立邪？

translations.literal: Shulü said in anger, "My son pacified Jin and took the realm—he achieved great merit; the son at my side ought to be enthroned, while the Human Emperor's son turned his back on me and went to China—how can his son be enthroned?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Shulü raged: "My son conquered Jin and won the realm with great merit; the son at my side should rule, yet the Human Emperor's heir forsook me for China—how can his son take the throne?"

sentences.zh: 」乃率兵逆兀欲，將廢之。

translations.literal: " She then led troops against Wuyu to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: " She marched against Wuyu to remove him.

sentences.zh: 兀欲留其將麻荅守鎮州，晉諸將相隨德光在鎮州者皆留之而去。

translations.literal: Wuyu left his general Mada to hold Zhen Prefecture; the Jin ministers and generals who had followed Deguang at Zhen were all detained as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu left his general Mada to guard Zhen Prefecture and detained the Jin officials who had accompanied Deguang there before setting out.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士徐台符、李澣從行，與其祖母述律相距于石橋。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan accompanied him; he met his grandmother Shulü at Shiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Xu Taifu and Li Huan went with him and confronted his grandmother Shulü at Shiqiao.

sentences.zh: 述律所將兵多亡歸兀欲。

translations.literal: Many of the troops Shulü led deserted back to Wuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Much of Shulü's army deserted to Wuyu.

sentences.zh: 兀欲乃幽述律於祖州。

translations.literal: Wuyu then imprisoned Shulü at Zuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu imprisoned Empress Dowager Shulü at Zuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖州，阿保機墓所也。

translations.literal: Zuzhou is where Abaoji's tomb lies.
translations.idiomatic: Zuzhou is the site of Abaoji's tomb.

sentences.zh: 述律為人多智而忍。

translations.literal: Shulü was by nature clever and ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was clever and pitiless.

sentences.zh: 阿保機死，悉召從行大將等妻，謂曰：「我今為寡婦矣，汝等豈宜有夫。

translations.literal: When Abaoji died, she summoned the wives of the great generals who had accompanied him and said, "I am now a widow—how can you still have husbands?"
translations.idiomatic: After Abaoji died she summoned the wives of the generals on the campaign and said, "I am a widow now—you should have no husbands either."

sentences.zh: 」乃殺其大將百餘人，曰：「可往從先帝。

translations.literal: " She then killed more than a hundred of their husbands, saying, "You may go join the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " She killed more than a hundred of those generals, saying, "Go join the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 」左右有過者，多送木葉山，殺於阿保機墓隧中，曰：「為我見先帝于地下。

translations.literal: " Those about her who offended were often sent to Mount Muye and killed in Abaoji's tomb passage, with the words, "Go see the late emperor for me in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: " Subordinates who erred were often sent to Mount Muye and slain in the tomb passage with the message, "Tell the late emperor I sent you.

sentences.zh: 」大將趙思溫，本中國人也，以材勇為阿保機所寵，述律後以事怒之，使送木葉山，思溫辭不肯行。

translations.literal: " The great general Zhao Siwen, originally a man of China, was favored by Abaoji for his talent and courage; later Shulü grew angry over some matter and ordered him sent to Mount Muye, but Siwen refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: " General Zhao Siwen, a Chinese by birth whom Abaoji favored for courage and skill, later angered her over some affair; when she ordered him to Mount Muye he refused.

sentences.zh: 述律曰：「爾，先帝親信，安得不往見之？

translations.literal: Shulü said, "You were the late emperor's trusted man—how can you fail to go see him?"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "You were the late emperor's intimate—will you not go to him?"

sentences.zh: 」思溫對曰：「親莫如后，后何不行？

translations.literal: Siwen replied, "No kin is closer than the empress—why does the empress not go?"
translations.idiomatic: Siwen answered, "No one was closer than the empress—why does the empress not go?"

sentences.zh: 」述律曰：「我本欲從先帝于地下，以子幼，國中多故，未能也。

translations.literal: Shulü said, "I originally meant to follow the late emperor underground, but because the heir was young and the realm had many troubles, I could not.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "I meant to follow him underground, but the heir was young and the state unsettled, so I could not.

sentences.zh: 然可斷吾一臂以送之。

translations.literal: Yet you may cut off one of my arms to send with you."
translations.idiomatic: Still, you may cut off one of my arms and send it with you."

sentences.zh: 」左右切諫之，乃斷其一腕，而釋思溫不殺。

translations.literal: Those at her side urgently remonstrated; she then cut off one wrist and released Siwen without killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants pleaded urgently; she severed one wrist instead and spared Siwen.

sentences.zh: 初，德光之擊晉也，述律常非之，曰：「吾國用一漢人為主可乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deguang attacked Jin, Shulü often opposed it, saying, "Can our state take a single Han as master?"
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang marched on Jin she had often objected: "Can our nation be ruled by a single Han?"

sentences.zh: 」德光曰「不可也。

translations.literal: Deguang said, "It cannot."
translations.idiomatic: Deguang answered, "It cannot."

sentences.zh: 」述律曰：「然則汝得中國不能有，後必有禍，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: Shulü said, "Then though you win China you cannot hold it; disaster will follow and regret will be useless."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "Then even if you seize China you cannot keep it; ruin will follow and regret will be too late."

sentences.zh: 」德光死，載其尸歸，述律不哭而撫其尸曰：「待我國中人畜如故，然後葬汝。

translations.literal: When Deguang died and his corpse was brought back, Shulü did not weep but stroked the body and said, "Wait until the people and livestock of our land are as before, then I will bury you."
translations.idiomatic: When Deguang died and his body was brought home, she did not weep but stroked the corpse: "When our people and herds are restored, then I will bury you."

sentences.zh: 」已而，兀欲囚之，後死于木葉山。

translations.literal: Before long Wuyu imprisoned her, and later she died at Mount Muye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wuyu imprisoned her, and she later died at Mount Muye.

sentences.zh: 兀欲更名阮，號天授皇帝，改元曰天祿。

translations.literal: Wuyu changed his name to Ruan, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Gift, and adopted the era name Tianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu took the name Ruan, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Gift, and proclaimed the era Tianlu.

sentences.zh: 是歲八月，葬德光於木葉山，遣人至鎮州召馮道、和凝等會葬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Deguang was buried at Mount Muye; envoys were sent to Zhen Prefecture to summon Feng Dao, He Ning, and others to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month Deguang was buried at Mount Muye, and messengers were sent to Zhen Prefecture to summon Feng Dao, He Ning, and others.

sentences.zh: 使者至鎮州，鎮州軍亂，大將白再榮等逐出麻荅。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Zhen Prefecture, the army there mutinied; the great general Bai Zairong and others drove Mada out.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys arrived to find Zhen Prefecture in revolt; Bai Zairong and other commanders expelled Mada.

sentences.zh: 據定州，已而悉其衆以北。

translations.literal: They held Ding Prefecture, then soon led all their forces north.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Ding Prefecture, then marched their entire force north.

sentences.zh: 麻荅者，德光之從弟也。

translations.literal: Mada was Deguang's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Mada was Deguang's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 德光滅晉，以為邢州節度使，元欲立，命守鎮州。

translations.literal: When Deguang destroyed Jin he was made Military Commissioner of Xing Prefecture; when Wuyu took the throne he was ordered to guard Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jin he became military commissioner of Xing; when Wuyu was enthroned he was left to hold Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 麻荅尤酷虐，多略中國人，剝面，抉目，拔髮，斷腕而殺之，出入常以鉗鑿挑割之具自隨，寢處前後掛人肝、脛、手、足，言笑自若，鎮、定之人不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Mada was especially cruel; he seized many Chinese, flayed their faces, gouged out eyes, plucked out hair, severed wrists, and killed them; he always carried pincers and chisels for picking and cutting, and before and behind his sleeping place hung human livers, shins, hands, and feet; he spoke and laughed as if at ease, and the people of Zhen and Ding could not endure the torment.
translations.idiomatic: Mada was savagely cruel: he seized Chinese captives, flayed faces, gouged eyes, tore out hair, severed wrists, and killed; he carried pincers and chisels everywhere, hung livers, shins, hands, and feet around his bed, and chatted calmly while the people of Zhen and Ding were tortured past endurance.

sentences.zh: 麻荅已去，馮道等乃南歸。

translations.literal: After Mada had gone, Feng Dao and the others returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mada had withdrawn, Feng Dao and his party went south again.

sentences.zh: 述律立，改元應曆，號天順皇帝，後更名璟。

translations.literal: Shulü took the throne, changed the era name to Yingli, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Accord, and later changed his name to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü succeeded him, adopted the era Yingli, styled himself Emperor of Heaven's Accord, and later renamed himself Jing.

sentences.zh: 述律有疾，不能近婦人，左右給事，多以宦者。

translations.literal: Shulü was ill and could not approach women; those who served him close at hand were mostly eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü was ill and could not be with women; his personal attendants were largely eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 然畋獵好飲酒，不恤國事，每酣飲，自夜至旦，晝則常睡，國人謂之「睡王」。

translations.literal: Yet he loved hunting and drinking, cared nothing for state affairs, and whenever he drank deeply he did so from night until dawn while sleeping by day; the people called him the "Sleep King."
translations.idiomatic: He loved the hunt and wine, neglected government, drank from night till dawn, and slept by day—the realm called him the Sleep King.

sentences.zh: 初，兀欲常遣使聘漢，使者至中國而周太祖入立。

translations.literal: Earlier Wuyu had often sent envoys to Han; the envoys reached China just as Zhou Taizu seized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu had often sent envoys to the Han court; they arrived just as Zhou Taizu took power.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣將軍朱憲報聘，憲還而兀欲死。

translations.literal: Taizu sent the general Zhu Xian in return; when Xian returned, Wuyu was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent General Zhu Xian on a return embassy; by the time Xian came back, Wuyu was dead.

sentences.zh: 述律立，遂不復南寇。

translations.literal: When Shulü took the throne he no longer raided south.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shulü was enthroned he ceased southern raids.

sentences.zh: 顯德六年夏，世宗北伐，以保大軍節度使田景咸為淤口關部署，右神武統軍李洪信為合流口部署，前鳳翔節度使王晏為益津關部署，侍衛親軍馬步都虞候韓通為陸路都部署。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Xiande, Shizong marched north; he made Baoda Army Commissioner Tian Jingxian commander at Yankou Pass, Right Divine Martial Commander Li Hongxin commander at the He-Liu mouth, former Fengxiang Commissioner Wang Yan commander at Yijin Pass, and Palace Guard Director Han Tong overall land commander.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth year of Xiande, Shizong marched north, appointing Tian Jingxian of Baoda to Yankou Pass, Li Hongxin of the Right Divine Martial Guard to the He-Liu mouth, Wang Yan, former Fengxiang commissioner, to Yijin Pass, and Han Tong, director of the palace guard, overall land commander.

sentences.zh: 世宗自乾寧軍御龍舟，艛船戰艦，首尾數十里，至益津關，降其守將，而河路漸狹，舟不能進，乃捨舟陸行。

translations.literal: Shizong himself sailed from Qianning on the imperial dragon boat with warships stretching for dozens of li; reaching Yijin Pass he accepted the surrender of its garrison, but the river route grew narrow and boats could not advance, so he left the fleet and marched by land.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sailed from Qianning on the imperial dragon boat with a fleet dozens of li long; at Yijin Pass the garrison surrendered, but the channel narrowed and the boats could go no farther, so he abandoned the river and marched overland.

sentences.zh: 瓦橋淤口關、瀛莫州守將，皆迎降。

translations.literal: The garrison commanders of Waqiao, Yankou, and Ying and Mo prefectures all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders at Waqiao, Yankou, and Ying and Mo prefectures all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 方下令進攻幽州，世宗遇疾，乃置雄州於瓦橋關、霸州於益津關而還。

translations.literal: Just as he ordered an attack on You Prefecture, Shizong fell ill; he then established Xiong Prefecture at Waqiao Pass and Ba Prefecture at Yijin Pass and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As he was ordering the assault on You Prefecture, Shizong fell ill; he set up Xiong Prefecture at Waqiao Pass and Ba Prefecture at Yijin Pass, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 周師下三關、瀛、莫，兵不血刃。

translations.literal: The Zhou army took the three passes and Ying and Mo without shedding blood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces took the three passes and Ying and Mo without bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 述律聞之，謂其國人曰：「此本漢地，今以還漢，又何惜耶？

translations.literal: When Shulü heard of it he told his people, "This was originally Han land; now that it is returned to Han, what is there to regret?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Shulü told his people, "This was always Han territory; now that Han has it back, why regret it?"

sentences.zh: 」述律後為庖者因其醉而殺之。

translations.literal: Later a cook killed Shulü while he was drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Later a kitchen servant killed him while he was drunk.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 自古夷狄服叛，雖不繫中國之盛衰，而中國之制夷狄則必因其彊弱。

translations.literal: From antiquity the submission and rebellion of the Yi and Di has never depended on whether China was flourishing or declining, yet China's control of the Yi and Di has always followed their strength or weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity whether the barbarians submit or rebel has not hinged on China's rise or fall, yet China's handling of them has always followed their strength.

sentences.zh: 予讀周日曆，見世宗取瀛、莫，定三關，兵不血刃，而史官譏其以王者之師，馳千里而襲人，輕萬乘之重於萑葦之間，以僥倖一勝。

translations.literal: Reading the Zhou Daily Calendar, I see that when Shizong took Ying and Mo and secured the three passes without bloodshed, the historians still mocked him for sending the army of a true king a thousand li to strike a foe, placing the weight of the imperial chariot among the reeds for the sake of a lucky victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou Daily Calendar I read that Shizong took Ying and Mo and fixed the three passes without a blow, yet the historians still scorned him for driving the royal host a thousand li to raid an enemy—risking the imperial carriage among the reeds for one lucky stroke.

sentences.zh: 夫兵法，決機因勢，有不可失之時。

translations.literal: In warfare one seizes the moment according to circumstance; there are times that cannot be missed.
translations.idiomatic: War turns on timing and circumstance; some moments cannot be lost.

sentences.zh: 世宗南平淮甸，北伐契丹，乘其勝威，擊其昏殆，世徒見周師之出何速，而不知述律有可取之機也。

translations.literal: Shizong had pacified the Huai region in the south and marched north against the Khitan, riding his victory to strike their confusion and weakness; the age only saw how swiftly the Zhou army marched, and did not know that Shulü offered a chance to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had pacified the Huai in the south and struck north against the Khitan on the momentum of victory, hitting their disorder and decay; men saw only how fast the Zhou marched, not that Shulü's court was ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 是時，述律以謂周之所取，皆漢故地，不足顧也。

translations.literal: At that time Shulü thought what Zhou seized was all old Han territory and not worth guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü then believed Zhou was merely recovering former Han lands and not worth defending.

sentences.zh: 然則十四州之故地，皆可指麾而取矣。

translations.literal: Then the old territory of the Fourteen Prefectures could all have been taken at a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: The Fourteen Prefectures might have been recovered at a wave of the hand.

sentences.zh: 不幸世宗遇疾，功志不就。

translations.literal: Unfortunately Shizong fell ill and his ambition was left unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Sadly Shizong fell ill and his design was cut short.

sentences.zh: 然瀛、莫、三關，遂得復為中國之人，而十四州之俗，至今陷於夷狄。

translations.literal: Yet Ying, Mo, and the three passes were restored to Chinese rule, while the people of the Fourteen Prefectures remain trapped among the barbarians to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Ying, Mo, and the three passes returned to China, while the folk of the Fourteen Prefectures remain under barbarian rule even now.

sentences.zh: 彼其為志豈不可惜，而其功不亦壯哉！

translations.literal: Was his aim not lamentable—and yet was his achievement not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: His purpose was cut short—yet what a bold achievement!

sentences.zh: 夫兵之變化屈伸，豈區區守常談者所可識也！

translations.literal: The flexing and bending of military affairs—how can pedants who cling to routine talk understand them!
translations.idiomatic: The twists of war are not for pedants who know only fixed formulas.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭翰聞德光死，北歸，有同州郃陽縣令胡嶠為翰掌書記，隨入契丹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiao Han heard Deguang was dead he went north; Hu Qiao of Heyang County in Tong Prefecture served Han as secretary and followed him into Khitan lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Han heard Deguang was dead he marched north; Hu Qiao, magistrate of Heyang in Tong Prefecture, had been Han's secretary and went with him into Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 而翰妻爭妒，告翰謀反，翰見殺，嶠無所依，居虜中七年。

translations.literal: Han's wife, jealous, accused Han of plotting rebellion; Han was killed, and Qiao had nowhere to turn and lived among the barbarians for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Han's wife, in jealousy, denounced him for rebellion; Han was executed, and Qiao, stranded, spent seven years among the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 當周廣順三年，亡歸中國，略能道其所見。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou he escaped back to China and could relate in outline what he had seen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's third year of Guangshun he fled home and could recount in outline what he had witnessed.

sentences.zh: 云：「自幽州西北入居庸關，明日，又西北入石門關，關路崖狹，一夫可以當百，此中國控扼契丹之險也。

translations.literal: He said: "From You Prefecture one goes northwest into Juyong Pass; the next day northwest again into Shimen Pass—the road narrow between cliffs, one man able to hold off a hundred; this is China's choke point against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "From You Prefecture we entered Juyong Pass to the northwest; next day Shimen Pass—the cliff road so narrow one man could hold a hundred; China's barrier against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又三日，至可汗州，南望五臺山，其一峰最高者，東臺也。

translations.literal: Three days more to Khan Prefecture; looking south one sees Mount Wutai, and the highest peak is the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Three days on to Khan Prefecture, with Mount Wutai to the south; its tallest peak is the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 又三日，至新武州，西北行五十里有雞鳴山，云唐太宗北伐聞雞鳴于此，因之名山。

translations.literal: Three days more to Xinwu Prefecture; fifty li northwest is Cockcrow Mountain—they say Tang Taizong on his northern campaign heard a cock crow here and named the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Three days more to Xinwu Prefecture; fifty li northwest stands Cockcrow Mountain, named because Tang Taizong heard a cock crow there on his northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 明日，入永定關，此唐故關也。

translations.literal: The next day he entered Yongding Pass—an old Tang pass.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Yongding Pass, an old Tang barrier.

sentences.zh: 又四日，至歸化州。

translations.literal: Four days more to Guihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Four days on to Guihua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又三日，登天嶺，嶺東西連亙，有路北下，四顧冥然，黃雲白草，不可窮極。

translations.literal: Three days more he climbed Heaven Ridge, which runs east and west; a road led down to the north, and on every side was dim emptiness—yellow clouds, white grass, without end.
translations.idiomatic: Three days more to Heaven Ridge, stretching east and west; a road dropped north into a dim expanse of yellow cloud and white grass without limit.

sentences.zh: 契丹謂嶠曰：『此辭郷嶺也，可一南望而為永訣。

translations.literal: The Khitan told Qiao, "This is the Ridge of Parting from Home—you may look once to the south and take your eternal farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan told him, "This is the Ridge of Parting from Home—look south once and bid farewell forever.

sentences.zh: 』同行者皆慟哭，往往絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: " Those traveling with him all wept bitterly, many fainting and reviving.
translations.idiomatic: " His companions wept until many fainted and woke again.

sentences.zh: 又行三四日，至黑榆林，時七月，寒如深冬。

translations.literal: Three or four days more to Black Poplar Grove—in the seventh month, cold as deep winter.
translations.idiomatic: Three or four days more to Black Poplar Grove, in the seventh month as cold as deep winter.

sentences.zh: 又明日，入斜谷，谷長五十里，高崖峻谷，仰不見日，而寒尤甚。

translations.literal: The next day he entered the Slanting Valley, fifty li long, with high cliffs and steep ravines where one could not see the sun overhead, and the cold was even worse.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the Slanting Valley, fifty li of towering cliffs and narrow gorge where the sun never showed and the cold was worse still.

sentences.zh: 已出谷，得平地，氣稍溫。

translations.literal: Having left the valley, they reached level ground and the air grew somewhat warmer.
translations.idiomatic: Out of the valley they found open ground and the air grew milder.

sentences.zh: 又行二日，渡湟水。

translations.literal: Two days more and they crossed the Huang River.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they forded the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 又明日，渡黑水。

translations.literal: The next day they crossed the Black River.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they crossed the Black River.

sentences.zh: 又二日，至湯城淀，地氣最溫，契丹若大寒，則就溫于此。

translations.literal: Two days more to Tangcheng Marsh, where the climate was warmest; when the Khitan suffered extreme cold they would seek warmth here.
translations.idiomatic: Two days on to Tangcheng Marsh, the warmest place in the land—when cold was fierce the Khitan wintered there.

sentences.zh: 其水泉清冷，草軟如茸，可藉以寢。

translations.literal: Its springs were clear and cold, the grass soft as fleece and fit to sleep on.
translations.idiomatic: The springs ran clear and cold, the turf soft as down, good for bedding.

sentences.zh: 而多異花，記其二種：一曰旱金，大如掌，金色爍人；

translations.literal: There were many strange flowers; he noted two kinds: one called dry gold, as large as the palm, its golden color dazzling;
translations.idiomatic: Strange flowers grew there; he named two: dry gold, palm-sized and dazzling gold;

sentences.zh: 一曰青囊，如中國金燈，而色類藍可愛。

translations.literal: one called green pouch, like China's golden lantern flower but with a lovely bluish hue.
translations.idiomatic: and green pouch, like China's golden lantern but tinged blue and lovely.

sentences.zh: 又二日，至儀坤州，渡麝香河。

translations.literal: Two days more to Yikun Prefecture, crossing the Musk River.
translations.idiomatic: Two days more brought Yikun Prefecture and a crossing of the Musk River.

sentences.zh: 自幽州至此無里候，其所向不知為南北。

translations.literal: From You Prefecture to here there were no mile markers, and one did not know which way was south or north.
translations.idiomatic: From You Prefecture onward there were no mile markers and no sense of direction.

sentences.zh: 又二日，至赤崖，翰與兀欲相及，遂及述律戰于沙河。

translations.literal: Two days more to Red Cliff; Han caught up with Wuyu, and they fought Shulü at the Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: Two days on to Red Cliff, where Han joined Wuyu and they battled Empress Dowager Shulü on the Sha River.

sentences.zh: 述律兵敗而北，兀欲追至獨樹渡，遂囚述律于撲馬山。

translations.literal: Shulü's army was defeated and fled north; Wuyu pursued to Dushu Ford and then imprisoned Shulü at Puma Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü was beaten and fled north; Wuyu chased her to Dushu Ford and imprisoned her at Puma Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又行三日、遂至上京，所謂西樓也。

translations.literal: Three days more and they reached the Upper Capital, called the Western Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later they reached the Upper Capital, known as the Western Tower.

sentences.zh: 西樓有邑屋市肆，交易無錢而用布。

translations.literal: The Western Tower had towns, houses, and market stalls; trade used cloth instead of coin.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Tower had streets, houses, and markets; they bartered in cloth, not coin.

sentences.zh: 有綾錦諸工作、宦者、翰林、伎術、教坊、角觝、秀才、僧、尼、道士等，皆中國人，而并、汾、幽、薊之人尤多。

translations.literal: There were brocade workshops, eunuchs, Hanlin scholars, artisans, music offices, wrestlers, examination candidates, monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and the like—all Chinese, with men from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade workshops stood beside eunuchs, Hanlin academicians, artisans, music schools, wrestlers, candidates, monks, nuns, and Daoists—almost all Chinese, especially from Bing, Fen, You, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 自上京東去四十里，至真珠寨，始食菜。

translations.literal: Forty li east from the Upper Capital one reached Pearl Stockade and could eat vegetables for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li east of the capital lay Pearl Stockade, where they first tasted greens.

sentences.zh: 明日，東行，地勢漸高，西望平地松林鬱然數十里。

translations.literal: The next day, traveling east, the ground rose gradually; looking west one saw level pine forest stretching densely for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they marched east over rising ground; to the west a level pine forest stretched tens of li.

sentences.zh: 遂入平川，多草木，始食西瓜，云契丹破回紇得此種，以牛糞覆棚而種，大如中國冬瓜而味甘。

translations.literal: They then entered a broad plain rich in grass and trees and first ate watermelon—they say the Khitan obtained the seed by defeating the Uyghurs, covered frames with cattle dung to grow it, and the fruit was as large as China's winter melon and sweet.
translations.idiomatic: They entered a fertile plain and first tasted watermelon—the Khitan said they took the seed from the Uyghurs, grew it under dung-heated frames, and the fruit rivaled China's winter melon in size and sweetness.

sentences.zh: 又東行，至褭潭，始有柳，而水草豐美，有息雞草尤美，而本大，馬食不過十本而飽。

translations.literal: Traveling east again they reached Niao Pool, where willows first appeared; water and grass were lush, and there was a grass called rest-chicken especially fine, with thick roots—a horse eating no more than ten stalks would be full.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east lay Niao Pool, the first willows, rich pasture, and rest-chicken grass so nourishing ten stalks filled a horse.

sentences.zh: 自褭潭入大山，行十餘日而出，過一大林，長二三里，皆蕪荑，枝葉有芒刺如箭羽，其地皆無草。

translations.literal: From Niao Pool they entered great mountains and traveled more than ten days before emerging; they passed a great forest two or three li long, all colewort, its branches and leaves bearing barbs like arrow feathers, and the ground beneath had no grass.
translations.idiomatic: From the pool they entered high mountains for ten-odd days, crossed a forest miles long of thorny colewort whose barbed leaves left the soil bare.

sentences.zh: 兀欲時卓帳于此，會諸部人葬德光。

translations.literal: Wuyu at that time pitched his tent here and gathered the tribes to bury Deguang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu had camped there to gather the tribes for Deguang's burial.

sentences.zh: 自此西南行，日六十里，行七日，至大山門，兩高山相去一里，而長松豐草，珍禽野卉，有屋室碑石，曰『陵所也。

translations.literal: From here they went southwest sixty li a day for seven days to Great Mountain Gate, two high peaks a li apart with long pines, rich grass, rare birds, and wild flowers; there were houses, steles, and stones, and it was said, "This is the mausoleum."
translations.idiomatic: Southwest sixty li a day for seven days brought Great Mountain Gate—two peaks a li apart, pine-clad, strewn with rare birds and flowers, with houses and inscribed stones marking the tomb.

sentences.zh: 』兀欲入祭，諸部大人惟執祭器者得入。

translations.literal: " Wuyu entered to offer sacrifice; only the tribal elders holding ritual vessels might enter.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyu entered to sacrifice; only elders bearing ritual vessels were admitted.

sentences.zh: 入而門闔。

translations.literal: Once inside, the gate was shut.
translations.idiomatic: The gate closed behind them.

sentences.zh: 明日開門，曰『拋盞』，禮畢。

translations.literal: The next day the gate opened in a rite called "Casting the Cup," and the ceremony was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the gate opened for the rite called Casting the Cup, and the service ended.

sentences.zh: 問其禮，皆祕不肯言。

translations.literal: When he asked about the ritual, all kept it secret and would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the rites, none would explain—they were secret.

sentences.zh: 」嶠所目見囚述律、葬德光等事，與中國所記差異。

translations.literal: " What Qiao saw with his own eyes—the imprisonment of Shulü, the burial of Deguang, and such matters—differed from China's records.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiao's eyewitness account of imprisoning Shulü, burying Deguang, and the like differed from Chinese records.

sentences.zh: 已而，翰得罪被鎖，嶠與部曲東之福州。

translations.literal: Before long Han offended and was put in chains; Qiao and his followers went east to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Han fell from favor and was chained; Qiao and his men went east to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 福州，翰所治也。

translations.literal: Fuzhou was where Han had governed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou was Han's former command.

sentences.zh: 嶠等東行，過一山，名十三山，云此西南去幽州二千里。

translations.literal: Qiao and his party traveled east, passed a mountain called Thirteen Mountains, and were told it lay two thousand li southwest of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling east they crossed Thirteen Mountains, said to stand two thousand li southwest of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又東行，數日，過衛州，有居人三十餘家，蓋契丹所虜中國衛州人，築城而居之。

translations.literal: Several days east they passed Weizhou, with a little more than thirty households—Chinese of Weizhou captured by the Khitan, who built a walled settlement and lived there.
translations.idiomatic: Days farther east lay Weizhou, a walled settlement of thirty-odd families—Chinese from Weizhou whom the Khitan had seized and resettled.

sentences.zh: 嶠至福州而契丹多憐嶠，教其逃歸，嶠因得其諸國種類遠近。

translations.literal: When Qiao reached Fuzhou many Khitan pitied him and taught him how to escape; he thereby learned the kinds of neighboring states and their distances.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou many Khitan pitied him and showed him how to flee; he thus learned the neighboring peoples and their distances.

sentences.zh: 云：「距契丹國東至于海，有鐵甸，其族野居皮帳，而人剛勇。

translations.literal: He said: "East of the Khitan state to the sea lies Tiedian; the tribe lives in the wild in leather tents, and the people are fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "East of Khitan to the sea lies Tiedian, a people in leather tents, fierce and bold.

sentences.zh: 其地少草木，水鹹濁，色如血，澄之乆而後可飲。

translations.literal: Their land has little vegetation; the water is brackish and turbid, colored like blood, and only after long settling may it be drunk.
translations.idiomatic: The land is bare; the water brackish and blood-red, drinkable only after long settling.

sentences.zh: 又東，女真，善射，多牛、鹿、野狗。

translations.literal: Farther east are the Jurchen, skilled archers, with many cattle, deer, and wild dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward are the Jurchen, fine archers, rich in cattle, deer, and wild dogs.

sentences.zh: 其人無定居，行以牛負物，遇雨則張革為屋。

translations.literal: They have no fixed dwellings, carry goods on oxen when traveling, and when it rains stretch hides for shelter.
translations.idiomatic: They have no fixed homes, load oxen when they move, and stretch hides for shelter in rain.

sentences.zh: 常作鹿鳴，呼鹿而射之，食其生肉。

translations.literal: They often imitate a deer's call, lure deer, shoot them, and eat the raw flesh.
translations.idiomatic: They mimic deer calls, lure the animals, shoot them, and eat the meat raw.

sentences.zh: 能釀糜為酒，醉則縛之而睡，醒而後解，不然，則殺人。

translations.literal: They can ferment millet into wine; when drunk they bind a man to sleep and release him only when sober—otherwise they kill.
translations.idiomatic: They brew millet wine; the drunk are bound until sober—otherwise they are killed.

sentences.zh: 又東南，渤海，又東，遼國，皆與契丹略同。

translations.literal: Southeast lies Bohai; east again the Liao state—all much like the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast lies Bohai; farther east the Liao state—both much like the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 其南海曲，有魚鹽之利。

translations.literal: Its southern sea bend has the profit of fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: On its southern coast are fish and salt.

sentences.zh: 又南，奚，與契丹略同，而人好殺戮。

translations.literal: South again are the Xi, much like the Khitan but fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: South are the Xi, similar to the Khitan but bloodthirsty.

sentences.zh: 又南，至于榆關矣，西南至儒州，皆故漢地。

translations.literal: South again one reaches Yuguan; southwest to Ru Prefecture—all old Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south is Yuguan; southwest to Ru Prefecture—all former Han lands.

sentences.zh: 西則突厥、回紇。

translations.literal: To the west are the Turks and Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: West lie the Turks and Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 西北至嫗厥律，其人長大，髦頭，酋長全其髮，盛以紫囊。

translations.literal: Northwest to Yujuelü—the people are tall, wear their hair loose, and chiefs keep their full hair bound in purple bags.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest is Yujuelü, whose people are tall and long-haired; chiefs keep their full locks in purple bags.

sentences.zh: 地苦寒，水出大魚，契丹仰食。

translations.literal: The land is bitterly cold; its waters yield great fish on which the Khitan rely for food.
translations.idiomatic: The country is frigid; great fish from its rivers feed the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又多黑、白、黃貂鼠皮，北方諸國皆仰足。

translations.literal: Black, white, and yellow sable pelts abound, and all northern states depend on them.
translations.idiomatic: Black, white, and yellow sable abound, and every northern realm depends on them.

sentences.zh: 其人最勇，鄰國不敢侵。

translations.literal: They are the bravest; neighboring states dare not invade.
translations.idiomatic: They are the fiercest warriors; neighbors dare not attack.

sentences.zh: 又其西，轄戛，又其北，單于突厥，皆與嫗厥律略同。

translations.literal: West again is Xiage; north again the Chanyu Turks—all much like Yujuelü.
translations.idiomatic: West again Xiage; north the Chanyu Turks—each like Yujuelü.

sentences.zh: 又北，黑車子，善作車帳，其人知孝義，地貧無所產。

translations.literal: North again the Black Cart people, skilled at making cart tents; they know filial duty, but the land is poor and produces nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north are the Black Cart people, makers of cart tents, dutiful but poor.

sentences.zh: 云契丹之先，常役回紇，後背之走黑車子，始學作車帳。

translations.literal: They say the Khitan ancestors long served the Uyghurs, then rebelled and fled to the Black Cart people and first learned to make cart tents.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan legend says their forebears served the Uyghurs, then fled north to the Black Cart folk and learned tent-making.

sentences.zh: 又北，牛蹄突厥，人身牛足，其地尤寒，水曰瓠

translations.literal: North again the Ox-hoof Turks, with human bodies and ox feet; the land is especially cold, and the river is called the Gourd
translations.idiomatic: North again the Ox-hoof Turks—human bodies, ox feet, bitter cold, and a river called the Gourd

sentences.zh: 〈盧瓜〉

translations.literal: 〈melon〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈melon〉

sentences.zh: 河，夏秋冰厚二尺，春冬冰徹底，常燒器銷冰乃得飲。

translations.literal: River; in summer and autumn the ice is two feet thick, in spring and winter frozen to the bottom, and they must melt ice in vessels by fire to obtain drink.
translations.idiomatic: River; in summer and autumn the ice is two feet thick, in spring and winter frozen solid, and they melt it over fire to drink.

sentences.zh: 東北，至襪劫子，其人髦首，披布為衣，不鞍而騎，大弓長箭，尤善射，遇人輒殺而生食其肉，契丹等國皆畏之。

translations.literal: Northeast to the Wajiezi—the people wear loose hair, dress in cloth, ride without saddles, carry great bows and long arrows, excel at shooting, kill anyone they meet and eat the flesh raw, and Khitan and other states all fear them.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast are the Wajiezi, long-haired, cloth-clad, saddleless riders with great bows; they kill on sight, eat raw flesh, and even the Khitan fear them.

sentences.zh: 契丹五騎遇一襪劫子，則皆散走。

translations.literal: When five Khitan horsemen meet one Wajiezi, they all scatter and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Five Khitan riders meeting one Wajiezi will scatter in flight.

sentences.zh: 其國三面皆室韋，一曰室韋，二曰黃頭室韋，三曰獸室韋。

translations.literal: Their state is bordered on three sides by Shiwei: first Shiwei, second Yellow-head Shiwei, third Beast Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan lands are ringed on three sides by Shiwei—the common, the Yellow-head, and the Beast Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 其地多銅、鐵、金、銀，其人工巧，銅鐵諸器皆精好，善織毛錦。

translations.literal: Their land has much copper, iron, gold, and silver; the people are clever artisans, and copper and iron wares are all fine; they weave wool brocade well.
translations.idiomatic: They have copper, iron, gold, and silver, skilled metalwork, and fine wool brocades.

sentences.zh: 地尤寒，馬溺至地成冰堆。

translations.literal: The land is extremely cold; horse urine freezes into heaps on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Cold is so fierce that horse urine freezes in heaps where it falls.

sentences.zh: 又北，狗國，人身狗首，長毛不衣，手搏猛獸，語為犬嗥，其妻皆人，能漢語，生男為狗，女為人，自相婚嫁，穴居食生，而妻女人食。

translations.literal: North again the Dog Country—human bodies with dog heads, long hair and no clothing, they wrestle beasts with their hands, their speech is canine howling, their wives are human and speak Chinese, sons are born dogs and daughters human, they marry among themselves, live in caves and eat raw food while their wives eat human food.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north is the Dog Country—men with dogs' heads and shaggy hides, howling speech, human wives who speak Chinese; sons are dogs, daughters human; they dwell in caves, eat raw meat, while wives eat cooked food.

sentences.zh: 云甞有中國人至其國，其妻憐之使逃歸，與其箸十餘隻，教其每走十餘里遺一箸，狗夫追之，見其家物，必銜而歸，則不能追矣。

translations.literal: They say a Chinese once reached their country; his wife pitied him and helped him escape, giving him more than ten chopsticks and teaching him to drop one every dozen li; when the dog-husband pursued and saw his household goods he would carry them back in his mouth and could not continue the chase.
translations.idiomatic: Legend tells of a Chinese captive whose wife pitied him, gave him chopsticks, and told him to drop one every dozen li—the dog-husband, seeing household goods, would carry them home and abandon the chase.

sentences.zh: 」其說如此。

translations.literal: " Such were their tales.
translations.idiomatic: " Such were the tales he heard.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「契丹甞選百里馬二十匹，遣十人齎乾

translations.literal: He also said: "The Khitan once chose twenty horses that could run a hundred li in a day and sent ten men carrying dried
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The Khitan once picked twenty hundred-li horses and sent ten men with dried

sentences.zh: 〈食少〉

translations.literal: 〈rations〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈rations〉

sentences.zh: 北行，窮其所見。

translations.literal: to march north and explore everything they could see.
translations.idiomatic: rations to march north and map all they could reach.

sentences.zh: 其人自黑車子，歷牛蹄國以北，行一年，經四十三城，居人多以木皮為屋，其語言無譯者，不知其國地、山川、部族、名號。

translations.literal: The men started from the Black Cart people, passed north through the Ox-hoof country, traveled a year, and passed forty-three walled settlements; most inhabitants built houses of tree bark, their speech had no interpreter, and their lands, mountains, tribes, and names were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: They set out from the Black Cart lands, crossed the Ox-hoof realm, traveled a year through forty-three bark-built towns whose speech none could interpret—country, mountains, tribes, and names unknown.

sentences.zh: 其地氣，遇平地則溫和，山林則寒冽。

translations.literal: The climate there: on level ground it was mild, in mountains bitter cold.
translations.idiomatic: On plains the air was mild; in mountains, biting cold.

sentences.zh: 至三十三城，得一人，能鐵甸語，其言頗可解，云地名頡利烏于邪堰。

translations.literal: At the thirty-third settlement they found one man who spoke Tiedian; his words could be partly understood, and he said the place was called Jieliwuyuxieyan.
translations.idiomatic: At the thirty-third town a man spoke Tiedian well enough to say the place was called Jieliwuyuxieyan.

sentences.zh: 云『自此以北，龍蛇猛獸、魑魅羣行，不可往矣』。

translations.literal: He said, "North of here dragons, serpents, fierce beasts, and demons roam in packs—you cannot go on."
translations.idiomatic: He warned, "Beyond lie dragons, serpents, beasts, and demons in throngs—no one may go farther."

sentences.zh: 其人乃還。

translations.literal: The men then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The party turned back.

sentences.zh: 此北荒之極也。」

translations.literal: This is the farthest north of the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: That was the limit of the northern wilds."

sentences.zh: 契丹謂嶠曰：「夷狄之人豈能勝中國？

translations.literal: The Khitan said to Qiao, "How could barbarians overcome China?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan told Qiao, "How could barbarians ever conquer China?

sentences.zh: 然晉所以敗者，主暗而臣不忠。

translations.literal: Yet Jin was defeated because its ruler was dim and his ministers disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell because its ruler was blind and his ministers faithless.

sentences.zh: 」因具道諸國事，曰：「子歸悉以語漢人，使漢人努力事其主，無為夷狄所虜，吾國非人境也。

translations.literal: " He then described the affairs of the various states in detail and said, "When you return, tell the Han everything so they will serve their lord diligently and not be captured by barbarians—our land is no place for men.
translations.idiomatic: " He described every realm and said, "Tell the Han on your return to serve their sovereign faithfully and avoid capture—our country is no human habitation.

sentences.zh: 」嶠歸，錄以為陷虜記云。

translations.literal: " When Qiao returned he recorded it as Captive's Record.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiao came home and wrote it up as the Captive's Record.
